## Purpose

`commands/wave/` owns every operation on a spec's wave-plan: parsing (`WaveTree`, `WaveDependency`), auditing (`WaveSizeCheck`, `WaveOverlapCheck`), and mutating (`wave_collapse.rs`, materializing/merging wave dirs). `cli.rs` is the family's `WaveCmd` enum + `dispatch()` following the crate-wide two-registration cli pattern; `wave_collapse.rs` is a representative mutating command with its own `*Opts` struct and atomic-write discipline.

## Convention

Folder: apps/rt/src/commands/wave/** · Extension: .rs · Files of this role in this subproject: 6

Every `--spec-dir`-taking wave command accepts the SAME three input spellings via clap aliases: `#[arg(long = "spec-dir", alias = "spec", alias = "from-spec")]` — a bare slug, a `.../spec.md` path, or a spec directory path, all resolved by the shared spec-dir resolver. Mutating commands (`wave_collapse.rs`) always write the merged/new content via `mfs::write_atomic` BEFORE deleting any surplus directory, so a crash never leaves a spec partially destroyed with no valid target; a missing precondition (no `wave-plan.md`) prints a `{"ok":false,"reason":"..."}` JSON and exits 0 rather than panicking.

## How to apply

Register the new wave verb as a `WaveCmd` variant with a `display_order` slot plus its `dispatch()` arm in `cli.rs`, accepting the `--spec-dir`/`--spec`/`--from-spec` alias triple when it takes a spec target. Reuse `crate::commands::spec::spec_sections::is_heading` for any locale-aware section lookup instead of hardcoding EN/pt-BR heading strings, and write mutations atomically in write-then-delete order.

## Examples

Ref: apps/rt/src/commands/wave/cli.rs
Ref: apps/rt/src/commands/wave/wave_collapse.rs

```rust
#[command(display_order = 18)]
WaveTree {
    #[arg(long = "spec-dir", alias = "spec", alias = "from-spec")]
    spec_dir: String,
    #[arg(long, default_value = "ascii")]
    format: String,
},
```
